mainTopic: When to mention rain (הזכרה) and when to ask for rain (שאלה) in תפילה: settling רבי יהודה's view, the practical הלכה, and the schedule for two days of יום טוב.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question: does the משנה follow only רבי יהושע? רבא answers that it can also fit רבי אליעזר, because asking for rain (שאלה) and mentioning rain (הזכרה) are two separate things. The גמרא then sets רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה against a ברייתא where he says we ask for rain until פסח has passed. רב חסדא tries to answer with the asking-versus-mentioning split, but עולא rejects it. עולא instead says two תנאים reported רבי יהודה's view differently. רב יוסף and then רבה each try to reread 'until פסח passes' so the two sources agree, but both readings are rejected, and the גמרא concludes twice that עולא is right. רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יהודה, and after several attempts the גמרא reconciles this with רבי אלעזר's ruling like רבן גמליאל. One date is for when the בית המקדש stands and the other for when it does not. Finally, רב and שמואל disagree about how people who keep two days of יום טוב should start mentioning rain.

steps.title: Does the משנה follow only רבי יהושע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes asking whether the משנה's ruling matches only רבי יהושע, who starts rain from the time the לולב is put down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the משנה following רבי יהושע, who said rain begins from the time the לולב is put down?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question that started just before this point. It asks whether the משנה must be following רבי יהושע and not רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע says rain begins when the לולב is put down, at the end of the חג. רבי אליעזר says it begins from when the לולב is taken, at the start of the חג. The משנה's ruling seems to fit only רבי יהושע, which would leave רבי אליעזר out.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who starts rain at the end of סוכות
From the time it (the לולב) is put down
The palm branch taken on סוכות; used here as a time marker

phrases.english: Is it the view of Rabbi Yehoshua,
who said: from the time of putting it down?!
phrases.notes: 'It' is the לולב, which is put down at the end of the חג.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הִיא, דְּאָמַר מִשְּׁעַת הַנָּחָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a question begun before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must the משנה follow רבי יהושע and not רבי אליעזר?

steps.title: רבא separates asking for rain from mentioning rain
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה can follow even רבי אליעזר, because שאלה (requesting rain) and הזכרה (mentioning rain) are separate matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can even say the משנה follows רבי אליעזר. Asking for rain is one thing, and mentioning rain is another.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. He shows that the משנה does not have to disagree with רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's early start is about mentioning rain, which is praising ה׳ as the One who brings rain. The משנה's ruling is about actually asking for rain. Since these are two different things, each can have its own start time, and both views fit.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say; it can fit even the other opinion
Requesting rain (in ברכת השנים)
Mentioning rain (משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם)
Separately, a distinct matter

steps.whatToRemember: שאלה (asking) and הזכרה (mentioning) are two separate parts of תפילה and can follow different timetables.
steps.whyThisMatters: This distinction is the key tool of the whole סוגיא, and רב חסדא uses it again below.

phrases.english: Rava said:
You can even say it follows Rabbi Eliezer —
requesting is separate, and mentioning is separate.
phrases.notes: Requesting means actually asking for rain. Mentioning means praising ה׳ as the One who brings rain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between two kinds of prayer (שאלה vs. הזכרה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's ruling clashes with רבי אליעזר's early start.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר's early start is about mentioning, and the משנה is about requesting, so they do not clash.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יהודה's ruling about the prayer leader
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: רבי יהודה rules about which prayer leader mentions rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: The one who passes before the ark... (and the rest of the משנה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting רבי יהודה's words from the משנה. This sets up the contradiction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה rules that on the first day of פסח the leader of שחרית mentions rain but the leader of מוסף does not. That means the mention of rain stops on the first day of פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose opinion is being examined
The one who passes before the ark: the שליח ציבור
Etc.: the rest of the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The one who passes before the ark, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: on the first day of פסח, שחרית mentions rain and מוסף does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הָעוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion on another line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the mention of rain stops on the first day of פסח, after שחרית.

steps.title: A ברייתא says רבי יהודה keeps asking for rain until after פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה says we ask for rain until פסח has passed, which seems to contradict the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contrasted it with a ברייתא: Until when do we ask for rain? רבי יהודה says: Until פסח has passed. רבי מאיר says: Until ניסן has passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction. In the ברייתא, רבי יהודה seems to say something different from what he says in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה stops rain on the first day of פסח. In the ברייתא, he continues until פסח is over. So which is his real opinion?

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it: introduces a contradicting source
Until when?
We ask (for rain)
The תנא who extends it to the end of ניסן

phrases.english: And they contrasted it:
Until when do we ask for rain?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיַּעֲבוֹר הַפֶּסַח,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Until Pesach has passed.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיַּעֲבוֹר נִיסָן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: Until Nisan has passed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's ruling quoted in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה that rain stops on the first day of פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same תנא, in a ברייתא, extends the rain until the end of פסח, which is a self-contradiction.

steps.title: רב חסדא: asking continues, mentioning stops
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא resolves the contradiction: the ברייתא is about asking for rain, which continues through פסח, and the משנה is about mentioning rain, which stops on the first day of יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This is not difficult. Here it is about asking, and there it is about mentioning. Asking continues on, but mentioning stops on the first day of יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the contradiction. Each source is talking about a different kind of prayer for rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the same split רבא used: שאלה versus הזכרה. In רבי יהודה's view, the request for rain goes on through פסח, while the mention ends on the first day. So both sources are correct.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the contradiction can be resolved
Here... there: each source deals with a different case
Continues asking
Stops

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב חסדא, רבי יהודה holds that we mention rain only until the first day of פסח but keep asking for rain until פסח is over. עולא rejects this in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two words: 'asking' (שאלה) and 'mentioning' (הזכרה) have different end dates here.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: It is not difficult:
Here it is about asking, there it is about mentioning.
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the ברייתא, which is about asking. 'There' is the משנה, which is about mentioning.

phrases.english: To ask, one keeps on asking,
to mention, one stops on the first day of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן לִשְׁאוֹל, כָּאן לְהַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: כאן וכאן: each source refers to a different kind of prayer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה gives two different end dates for the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about asking, which lasts through פסח. The משנה is about mentioning, which stops on the first day of יום טוב.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In רב חסדא's reading, רבי יהודה ends the mention of rain on the first day of פסח but continues the request until פסח is over. עולא rejects this reading in step 6.

steps.title: עולא rejects רב חסדא's answer with a logical argument
steps.stepSummary: עולא calls רב חסדא's answer as hard to swallow as vinegar on the teeth. If we mention rain even before we ask for it, then surely we should mention rain while we are still asking for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: רב חסדא's answer is as hard to take as vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes. Think about it: at a time when a person is not yet asking for rain, he already mentions rain. So at a time when he is asking for rain, shouldn't he surely mention it?
steps.whatsHappening: עולא attacks רב חסדא's answer from step 5. He argues that it makes no sense to keep asking for rain while you have already stopped mentioning it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the start of the rainy season we begin mentioning rain (משיב הרוח) before we begin asking for it (ותן טל ומטר). So mentioning is the 'easier' or broader practice. If mentioning comes even without asking, then whenever we ask, we should surely mention too. רב חסדא's split, where we ask but don't mention during פסח, flips this logic upside down.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who raises the challenge here
Like vinegar to the teeth: a phrase from משלי for something very unpleasant
'Now if...': opens a קל וחומר argument
'Isn't it logical...?': finishes the קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two terms. מַזְכִּיר means mentioning God's power over rain ('משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם'). שׁוֹאֵל means actually asking for rain ('ותן טל ומטר'). עולא's whole argument rests on mentioning starting earlier than asking.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
That answer of Rav Chisda is difficult,
like vinegar to the teeth and like smoke to the eyes.
Now if, in a situation where one does not ask for rain, he still mentions it,
phrases.notes: This is the start of the rainy season, when we already say משיב הרוח but have not started asking yet.

phrases.aramaic: בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁשּׁוֹאֵל, אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיְּהֵא מַזְכִּיר?
phrases.english: then in a situation where one does ask, isn't it logical that he should mention it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא קַשְׁיָא כַּחֹמֶץ לַשִּׁנַּיִם וְכֶעָשָׁן לָעֵינָיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's resolution in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's distinction that asking continues through פסח while mentioning stops on the first day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: mentioning happens even when there is no asking, so whenever there is asking there should surely be mentioning

steps.title: עולא: two traditions of רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: Since רב חסדא's answer fails, עולא resolves the contradiction differently. Two תנאים disagreed about what רבי יהודה held.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, עולא said: there are two תנאים who reported different opinions in the name of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives his own answer to the contradiction. The משנה and the ברייתא simply reflect two different reports of רבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of finding a way to make both sources agree, עולא admits they really disagree. One תנא held that רבי יהודה both mentions and asks through פסח. The other held that he stops both on the first day. This way nobody has to keep asking without mentioning.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather': drops the earlier answer and offers a new one
Two תנאים, meaning two early teachers
According to the view of

steps.whyThisMatters: 'Two תנאים according to so-and-so' is a common way the גמרא settles a contradiction it cannot otherwise resolve. It treats the two sources as two separate traditions.

phrases.english: Rather, Ulla said:
There are two tanna'im who disagree about the view of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב חסדא's rejected answer with a new resolution
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two separate traditions of the same תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources reflect one consistent view of רבי יהודה, so some distinction must reconcile them
steps.terutzMaskana: The sources really disagree; they are two different reports of רבי יהודה's view

steps.title: רב יוסף reinterprets 'until Pesach passes'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reads the ברייתא's words 'until פסח passes' to mean until the first prayer leader of the first day of פסח has finished. Then the ברייתא and the משנה agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: what does 'until פסח passes' mean? It means until the first שליח ציבור who goes down to lead prayers on the first יום טוב of פסח has finished.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a third answer to the contradiction from step 4. He rereads the ברייתא's wording so it matches the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seemed to say asking continues through all of פסח. רב יוסף says 'pass' refers to the first prayer leader passing before the ark on the first day. So both sources end at the same point, and there is no contradiction and no need for רב חסדא's split.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא offering another answer
Until it passes: the words being reinterpreted
The prayer leader who leads the congregation
Who goes down, meaning who steps up to lead prayers before the ark

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
What does 'until Pesach passes' mean?
Until the first prayer leader passes,

phrases.aramaic: הַיּוֹרֵד בְּיוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח.
phrases.english: the one who goes down to lead prayers on the first Festival day of Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר מַאי עַד שֶׁיַּעֲבוֹר הַפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another way to resolve the step 4 contradiction, instead of עולא's two-תנאים approach
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Until פסח passes' means until the whole festival is over
steps.terutzMaskana: It means until the first prayer leader of the first day finishes, which matches the משנה

steps.title: אביי: there is no asking for rain on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף: asking for rain is not said on יום טוב at all. So how can the ברייתא say we ask until a point on the first day of יום טוב?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: is there any asking for rain on יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's new reading. On יום טוב we never ask for rain, so the ברייתא could not be describing asking for rain up to that day's prayers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The request for rain is part of ברכת השנים, a weekday blessing in the עמידה. On שבת and יום טוב that blessing is not said. Since asking had already stopped on the weekdays before פסח, saying 'we ask until the first day's prayer leader passes' adds nothing. That makes רב יוסף's reading hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא and student of רב יוסף, who challenges him here
Asking: the actual request for rain
'Is there...?': a question expecting the answer 'no'

steps.confusionAlert: Asking for rain belongs to the weekday עמידה only. The יום טוב עמידה has no ברכת השנים, so no asking for rain is ever said in it.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Is there any asking for rain on a Festival?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי שְׁאֵלָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב מִי אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's reinterpretation in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's reading that asking for rain lasts until the first prayer leader of the first day of פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Asking for rain is never said on יום טוב, so the ברייתא could not mean asking ends at a point on the first day of יום טוב

steps.title: The translator is the one who asks
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers אביי: yes, the asking happens on the first day of פסח. But it is not in the עמידה. The מתורגמן says it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes, it is the מתורגמן who asks for rain.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his reading against אביי's question. He says the 'asking' on the first day of פסח is done by the מתורגמן, not in the עמידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי asked how there could be asking for rain on יום טוב, since the עמידה of יום טוב has no request for rain. רב יוסף moves the asking out of the עמידה and gives it to the public announcer and translator. That way his reading of the ברייתא can still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
The public translator and announcer who spoke to the crowd for the speaker
Asks, here meaning makes the request for rain

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is answering אביי's question from the last step.

phrases.english: the translator asks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines who does the asking: the מתורגמן, not the עמידה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Asking until the first day of פסח must mean asking in the עמידה of יום טוב, which does not exist
steps.terutzMaskana: The asking on the first day is done by the מתורגמן

steps.title: No one asks for what the community does not need
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב יוסף's answer. Why would the מתורגמן ask for rain on פסח, when rain is no longer wanted then?
steps.simpleTranslation: But would a מתורגמן ask for something the community does not need?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יוסף's new defense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By פסח the rainy season is over, and rain is not needed. A מתורגמן speaks for the people, so he would not ask for something they do not want. This knocks out רב יוסף's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: But would...? (a doubtful, rhetorical question)
The community

phrases.english: But would a translator ask for
something the community does not need?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מְתוּרְגְּמָן שׁוֹאֵל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לַצִּבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's defense in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the מתורגמן asks for rain on the first day of פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A request for rain on פסח makes no sense, because the community no longer wants rain

steps.title: Back to עולא's answer
steps.stepSummary: Since רב יוסף's reading failed, the גמרא concludes that עולא's answer is the clear one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear: the answer is like עולא said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב יוסף's approach. It goes back to עולא: two תנאים disagreed about what רבי יהודה held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא did not try to make the ברייתא and the משנה agree. He said they report two different versions of רבי יהודה's view. Once the attempts to harmonize them fail, that answer is left standing.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we drop the last idea)
It is clear, the plain conclusion
Like עולא said

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear: it is as עולא said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes after רב יוסף's answer collapses
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא and the משנה reflect two versions of רבי יהודה, as עולא said

steps.title: Until the time of slaughtering the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבה offers a new reading. 'Until פסח passes' means until the afternoon of the 14th of ניסן, when the קרבן פסח is slaughtered. After that we stop asking, but we keep mentioning rain until the next morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: What does 'until פסח passes' mean? Until the time of slaughtering the קרבן פסח has passed. The end works like the beginning. At the beginning of the season we mention rain even though we do not ask for it yet. So too at the end, we mention rain even though we no longer ask for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a new way to make the ברייתא match the משנה. He reads 'פסח' as the קרבן פסח, not the holiday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If asking ends on ערב פסח, the ברייתא no longer says we ask on יום טוב. Mentioning can then last until the first prayer of יום טוב, as the משנה says. רבה backs this up with a pattern: in the fall, mentioning starts before asking, so in the spring mentioning can end after asking.

keyTerms.meaning: Until פסח passes
The slaughtering of the קרבן פסח, on the afternoon of 14 ניסן
Its end is like its beginning
Mentions rain (מַשִּׁיב הָרוּחַ), as opposed to asking for it

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two actions apart. Mentioning (praising ה׳ as the one who brings rain) is not the same as asking (requesting rain). רבה's whole idea depends on the two having different start and end points.

phrases.english: רבה said:
What does "until פסח passes" mean?
Until the time of slaughtering the Pesach offering passes.
And its end is like its beginning:
Just as at its beginning

phrases.aramaic: מַזְכִּיר אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ שׁוֹאֵל,
phrases.english: one mentions rain even though one does not ask,
so too at its end

phrases.aramaic: מַזְכִּיר אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ שׁוֹאֵל.
phrases.english: one mentions rain even though one does not ask.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר: מַאי עַד שֶׁיַּעֲבוֹר הַפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new attempt to reconcile the ברייתא and the משנה after רב יוסף's attempt failed
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets a word: 'פסח' means the קרבן פסח
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Until פסח passes' means through the holiday, which clashes with the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: Asking ends on ערב פסח. Mentioning continues into the first day, just as mentioning starts before asking in the fall

steps.title: Mentioning at the end has no purpose
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבה's pattern. Mentioning before asking makes sense as a warm-up for the request, but mentioning after asking has ended prepares for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: It makes sense that at the beginning one mentions rain, because mentioning is a kind of warm-up before the request. But at the end, what request is there to warm up for?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the comparison that רבה's answer rests on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mentioning in the fall has a reason: it praises ה׳ and prepares the way for the request that will soon follow. In the spring no request is coming, so there is no reason to keep mentioning. The beginning and the end are not alike, so רבה's comparison fails.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that... (granting one side before challenging the other)
Winning favor before a request, a warm-up for it
There is

phrases.english: אביי said to him:
It makes sense that at the beginning one mentions rain,
because mentioning is also a warm-up for the request,
but at the end,
what warm-up for a request is there?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: בִּשְׁלָמָא תְּחִילָּתוֹ מַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's reasoning in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's comparison 'its end is like its beginning'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mentioning before asking prepares for the request. After asking ends there is nothing to prepare for, so the two cases are not alike

steps.title: Again, עולא's answer stands
steps.stepSummary: With רבה's reading rejected, the גמרא again concludes that עולא's answer is the clear one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear: the answer is like עולא said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the whole set of attempts and goes back to עולא's answer a second time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two tries at reading the ברייתא so it fits the משנה have now failed: רב יוסף's and רבה's. The final answer is that the two sources hold two different versions of רבי יהודה's view.
steps.whatToRemember: Every attempt to make the ברייתא ('until פסח passes') agree with the משנה ('stop on the first day of פסח') failed. The final answer is עולא's: two תנאים reported רבי יהודה's view differently.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear: it is as עולא said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes after רבה's answer is rejected
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עולא's answer of two versions of רבי יהודה is the accepted resolution

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from explaining the sources to deciding the practical הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that רבי יהודה's view has been discussed, רבי יוחנן rules that we follow it. This ruling is about to be tested in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows...

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: רבי אסי said that רבי יוחנן said:
The הלכה follows רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about the practical ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה regarding mentioning rain

steps.title: רבי זירא doubts the report about רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks whether רבי יוחנן really said this. רבי יוחנן's student רבי אלעזר ruled like רבן גמליאל, who starts asking for rain only on the seventh of מרחשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי אסי: Did רבי יוחנן really say that? But we learned in a משנה: On the third of מרחשון we ask for rain. רבן גמליאל says: on the seventh of it. And רבי אלעזר said: The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges רבי אסי's report. He points to another ruling from the same circle, רבי אלעזר, which seems to point the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא assumes that ruling like רבי יהודה ties asking closely to mentioning, which starts on שמיני עצרת. רבן גמליאל delays asking until the seventh of מרחשון. רבי זירא sees these as clashing, so he doubts רבי יוחנן said it.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say that? (a challenge to a reported statement)
But we learned in a משנה...
The month after תשרי
We ask for rain

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: רבי זירא said to רבי אסי:
And did רבי יוחנן really say that?
But we learned: On the third of מרחשון
we ask for rain.
רבן גמליאל says: on the seventh of it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל!
phrases.english: And רבי אלעזר said: The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל!
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר was רבי יוחנן's leading student, so his ruling is taken to show what רבי יוחנן held.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the report in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's report that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's student ruled like רבן גמליאל, who delays asking for rain to 7 מרחשון. This seems to clash with ruling like רבי יהודה, so the report is doubted

steps.title: A student does not have to follow his teacher
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי answers רבי זירא: you cannot set one person's ruling against another person's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are you setting one man against another man?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי pushes back on רבי זירא's question. רבי אלעזר is a different person from רבי יוחנן, so they are allowed to rule differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's question assumed that a student would always hold like his teacher. רבי אסי rejects that assumption, so there is nothing to explain. Even so, the גמרא will go on to offer answers that keep the two rulings in agreement.

keyTerms.meaning: one man against another man
you are raising a contradiction

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי אסי is answering רבי זירא here.

phrases.english: Are you setting one man against another man?!
phrases.notes: He means that רבי אלעזר, even though he is a student, can rule differently from his teacher רבי יוחנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's contradiction from step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies that the two sources must agree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר must hold like his teacher רבי יוחנן
steps.terutzMaskana: Two different אמוראים may simply disagree

steps.title: One ruling is about asking, the other about mentioning
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: רבי אלעזר's ruling is about asking for rain, and רבי יוחנן's ruling is about mentioning rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is not difficult: here it is about asking, there it is about mentioning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to make the rulings fit together. Each ruling deals with a different part of the prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mentioning rain (משיב הרוח) could begin on שמיני עצרת, following רבי יהודה. Asking for rain (ותן טל ומטר) could begin on the seventh of מרחשון, following רבן גמליאל. With this split, teacher and student no longer disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: if you want, say (introduces another answer)
to ask (the request for rain)
to mention (the praise of rain)

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two terms apart. 'Mentioning' (הזכרה) is praising ה׳ as the one who brings rain. 'Asking' (שאלה) is the actual request for rain.

phrases.english: If you want, say: it is not difficult:
here it is about asking, there it is about mentioning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same contradiction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings concern the same part of the prayer
steps.terutzMaskana: Mentioning starts on שמיני עצרת and asking starts on the seventh of מרחשון

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says we mention whenever we ask
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the split by quoting רבי יוחנן: at the time one asks, one mentions.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יוחנן say: at the time one asks, one mentions!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the previous answer using another statement of רבי יוחנן himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If asking and mentioning go together, they cannot start on different dates. That seems to cancel the split between asking and mentioning.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't he say? (introduces a challenge)
at the point where one asks

phrases.english: But didn't רבי יוחנן say:
At the time one asks, one mentions!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The split between asking and mentioning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן links asking and mentioning, so they cannot start at different times

steps.title: That statement was about stopping
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן's link between asking and mentioning was said only about when they stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: That was said about stopping.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רבי יוחנן's statement so the split from step 19 can survive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking and mentioning stop together, but they could still begin on different days. So רבי יוחנן's statement does not rule out a later start for asking.

keyTerms.meaning: stopping
it was said

phrases.english: That was said about stopping.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the quoted statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Asking and mentioning are linked at both the start and the end
steps.terutzMaskana: They are linked only at the end

steps.title: רבי יוחנן links them at the start too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a fuller statement of רבי יוחנן: when one starts mentioning, one starts asking, and when one stops asking, one stops mentioning.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יוחנן say: when one begins to mention, one begins to ask; when one stops asking, one stops mentioning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a clearer statement from רבי יוחנן that knocks down the asking and mentioning answer completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This statement explicitly links the start as well as the end. So the 'only about stopping' answer fails, and the split from step 19 collapses.

keyTerms.meaning: began
stopped

phrases.english: But didn't רבי יוחנן say:
When one began to mention, one begins to ask;
when one stopped asking, one stops mentioning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer in step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן linked asking and mentioning only at the end
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן explicitly links the start as well

steps.title: One ruling for us in בבל, one for them in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: A new answer: רבי אלעזר's ruling like רבן גמליאל is for בבל, and רבי יוחנן's ruling is for ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is not difficult: this is for us, that is for them.
steps.whatsHappening: Having dropped the asking and mentioning split, the גמרא splits the rulings by place instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בבל people wait longer to ask for rain, which matches רבי אלעזר's ruling. In ארץ ישראל people start right away, which matches רבי יוחנן's ruling. Since the two places differ, the rulings do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (drops the earlier answer)
this is for us (in בבל), that is for them (in ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:
this is for us, and that is for them.
phrases.notes: 'Us' means the people of בבל, where the גמרא is speaking. 'Them' means the people of ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא לַן, הָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that failed in step 22
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings apply in the same place
steps.terutzMaskana: רבן גמליאל's date is for בבל, and the earlier date is for ארץ ישראל

steps.title: ארץ ישראל has its own reason to wait
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes בבל different. We have fruit in the fields, but ארץ ישראל has pilgrims traveling home.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about us? That we have fruit in the field. They also have pilgrims!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the location split by showing that ארץ ישראל also has a reason to delay asking for rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בבל waits because fruit is still out in the fields and rain would hurt it. ארץ ישראל also needs dry weather so the pilgrims can travel home. So the location difference does not explain why ארץ ישראל would start right away.

keyTerms.meaning: what is different?
fruit in the field
pilgrims who went up for the festival

phrases.english: What is different about us?
That we have fruit in the field.

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידְהוּ נָמֵי אִית לְהוּ עוֹלֵי רְגָלִים!
phrases.english: They also have pilgrims!
phrases.notes: The people who came to ירושלים for סוכות need dry roads for their trip home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the location split in step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ארץ ישראל asks for rain right after the festival
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ארץ ישראל has a reason to delay that is just as strong as בבל's

steps.title: רבי יוחנן spoke about a time without the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן's ruling refers to the time when the בית המקדש is not standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יוחנן said it, it was for the time when the בית המקדש is not standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the pilgrim problem by limiting רבי יוחנן's ruling to a time when there is no בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a בית המקדש there are no pilgrims, so ארץ ישראל can ask for rain right away. That removes the challenge from step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: the בית המקדש is standing
when he said it

phrases.english: When רבי יוחנן said it,
it was for the time when the בית המקדש is not standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pilgrim challenge in step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ruling to a time period
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's ruling applies even when there are pilgrims
steps.terutzMaskana: It applies only when there is no בית המקדש and therefore no pilgrims

steps.title: Both rulings are for ארץ ישראל, split by the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: Building on the last answer, the גמרא concludes that both rulings are for ארץ ישראל. The later date applies when the בית המקדש stands, and the earlier date applies when it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, both this and that are for them, and it is not difficult: here it is when the בית המקדש is standing, there it is when the בית המקדש is not standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sees that the last answer allows a simpler solution, and it gives its final resolution of the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need to split between בבל and ארץ ישראל anymore. In ארץ ישראל itself, people waited until the seventh of מרחשון when pilgrims were traveling home, which is רבן גמליאל's view. Today, with no pilgrims, they ask right away, which is רבי יוחנן's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: now that you have come to this
both this and that

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer is that רבן גמליאל's later date fits the time of the בית המקדש, when pilgrims needed dry roads. The earlier date fits a time without the בית המקדש. Both rulings are about ארץ ישראל.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the date for asking for rain depends on the real needs of the people, such as travelers and crops.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
this and that are both for them, and it is not difficult:
here it is when the בית המקדש is standing,

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים.
phrases.english: there it is when the בית המקדש is not standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 25 to replace the location split from step 23
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both rulings apply in ארץ ישראל. Wait until the seventh of מרחשון when the בית המקדש stands, and ask right away when it does not.

steps.title: What do people with two days of יום טוב do?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how people in חוץ לארץ, who keep two days of יום טוב, should start mentioning rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we, who have two days of יום טוב, how do we act?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question about people living outside ארץ ישראל who keep two days of יום טוב. This sets up the next steps, where רב and שמואל each give an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain is first mentioned on שמיני עצרת. In חוץ לארץ, however, the first day of שמיני עצרת might really be the seventh day of סוכות. So it is unclear exactly when to start.

keyTerms.meaning: And we, meaning the speakers in בבל
Two days of יום טוב
How do we act? What do we do?

phrases.english: And we, who have two days,
phrases.notes: He means two days of יום טוב, which are kept outside ארץ ישראל because of doubt about the date.

phrases.english: how do we act?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲנַן דְּאִית לַן תְּרֵי יוֹמֵי, הֵיכִי עָבְדִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the dates for ארץ ישראל are settled, the גמרא turns to communities that keep two days of יום טוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: On which day and at which prayer should people who keep two days of יום טוב start mentioning rain?

steps.title: רב's schedule: start, stop, start again
steps.stepSummary: רב says to begin mentioning rain at מוסף of the first day, stop at מנחה, ערבית and שחרית, and resume at מוסף of the second day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: One begins at מוסף, stops at מנחה, ערבית and שחרית, and goes back to mentioning at מוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question with a back-and-forth schedule for mentioning rain over the two days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At מוסף of the first day, he treats the day as שמיני עצרת and begins mentioning rain. From מנחה on, he worries the day might really be the seventh day of סוכות, so he stops. At מוסף of the second day, which is surely שמיני עצרת, he begins again.

keyTerms.meaning: Begins mentioning rain
Stops mentioning rain
Goes back and does it again
The מוסף prayer

phrases.english: Rav said: One begins at the additional prayers,
phrases.notes: This is מוסף of the first day of שמיני עצרת.

phrases.english: and stops at the afternoon, evening and morning prayers,
phrases.notes: מנחה is on the first day; ערבית and שחרית belong to the second day.

phrases.english: and goes back to it at the additional prayers.
phrases.notes: This is מוסף of the second day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Begin at מוסף of day one, pause from מנחה through שחרית of day two, and resume at מוסף of day two.

steps.title: שמואל objects: you cannot make it holy and then ordinary
steps.stepSummary: שמואל sends a message to רב: after treating the day as holy, how can you then treat it as ordinary?
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to them: Go out and tell Abba: After you made it holy, will you make it ordinary?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל challenges רב's schedule by pointing out that it contradicts itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By mentioning rain at מוסף, רב treated the day as שמיני עצרת, a holy day of its own. When he stops at מנחה, he is treating that same day as if it were still part of סוכות. You cannot switch your view of the same day halfway through.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out
רב's personal name
Holy
Ordinary, not holy

phrases.english: Shmuel said to them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the people who told שמואל what רב had said.

phrases.english: Go out and tell Abba:
After you have made it holy,
will you make it ordinary?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's answer from step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling to stop mentioning rain at מנחה of the first day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Starting at מוסף treats the day as שמיני עצרת. Stopping at מנחה treats the same day as סוכות. This is a contradiction within one day.

steps.title: שמואל's schedule: keep going through מנחה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says to begin at מוסף and continue at מנחה of the first day, stop at ערבית and שחרית, and resume at מוסף of the second day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, שמואל said: One begins at מוסף and at מנחה, stops at ערבית and שחרית, and goes back and begins at מוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל offers his own answer to the question from step 27, fixing the problem he raised against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רב, שמואל keeps mentioning rain at מנחה, so the first day is treated the same way all day long. The pause only comes at ערבית and שחרית, which belong to the next day, and mentioning resumes at מוסף of the second day.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a different answer
And at the מנחה prayer too

steps.whatToRemember: רב stops mentioning rain starting at מנחה of the first day. שמואל says to keep mentioning it through מנחה, because a day you treated as holy cannot become ordinary. Both agree there is a pause at ערבית and שחרית and that mentioning resumes at מוסף of the second day.
steps.confusionAlert: The only difference between רב and שמואל is מנחה of the first day. Everything else in the two schedules is the same.

phrases.english: Rather, Shmuel said:
One begins at the additional prayers and at the afternoon prayer,
and stops at the evening and morning prayers,
and goes back and begins at the additional prayers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רב's schedule in step 29, שמואל gives his own answer to step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Mention rain at מוסף and מנחה of day one, pause at ערבית and שחרית, and resume at מוסף of day two.
